## Activity

During January 2022, Central Eye Clinic completed 150 captures. Activity was carried out as part of the clinic’s routine operational work, with session lists running as planned apart from routine leave. The recorded volume provides the basis for reviewing image quality and the subsequent grading outcomes for the month. No operational issue was identified in the available activity information that would require separate escalation.

## Image quality

There were 2 ungradable captures during the reporting period. The ungradable rate was 1.3 per cent. This indicates that almost all images obtained were suitable for review, while the small number that could not be graded should continue to be monitored through routine quality assurance. The result should be considered alongside the total of 150 captures completed at the site.

## Grading

Grading identified 35 referable results. The median lag from capture to grading was 17 days. This measure provides an overview of the time taken for images to progress through the grading process and should be reviewed routinely with activity and image-quality findings. Overall, the report records completed activity, a low ungradable rate, and the referable outcomes identified through grading at Central Eye Clinic.
